tasks.title: Apply all the functions
tasks.statement: Write a function apply_all(funcs, x): a list of the results of calling each function from funcs on x, in the same order.
tasks.hint: Functions are ordinary values: [f(x) for f in funcs].

tasks.title: Longest first
tasks.statement: Write a function by_length_desc(words): the words from the longest to the shortest; words of the same length keep their original order. Use sorted and lambda.
tasks.hint: sorted(words, key=lambda w: len(w), reverse=True): the sort is stable even with reverse.

tasks.title: The oldest
tasks.statement: Write a function oldest(users): users is a list of dictionaries {'name': ..., 'age': ...}. Return the name of the oldest. The list is not empty. Use max with the key parameter.

tasks.title: map and filter
tasks.statement: Write a function even_squares(nums): a LIST of the squares of the even numbers, in the original order. Solve it with filter and map (with lambda), and then wrap the result in list.
tasks.hint: list(map(lambda x: x * x, filter(lambda x: x % 2 == 0, nums))).

tasks.title: Function composition
tasks.statement: Write a function compose(f, g): it returns a new function that first applies g, and then f to the result: compose(f, g)(x) == f(g(x)).

tasks.title: How many arguments
tasks.statement: Write a function describe(*args, **kwargs): it returns a string like "2 positional, 1 named": how many positional and how many keyword arguments were received.

tasks.title: Pure append
tasks.statement: Write a pure function pure_append(items, x): it returns a NEW list with x added, without changing the original.
tasks.hint: return items + [x]: the plus operator creates a new list.

tasks.title: Product with reduce
tasks.statement: Write a function product(nums): the product of all the numbers in the list, and 1 for an empty list. Use reduce from functools with an initial value.
tasks.hint: reduce(lambda acc, x: acc * x, nums, 1): one as the initial value gives 1 for an empty list.
